decisions.reason: As a close-to-core cardboard display variant with low carrying cost and no clear sign of failure, it still has option value for future customer projects.
This pegboard-backed display is an incremental extension of the firm's established offer, so a large German display producer would likely retain it while demand remains somewhat uncertain.
Although it overlaps with other quarter-pallet formats, it is still a core cardboard product whose low maintenance cost supports keeping the option open.
The eighth-pallet format serves a distinct footprint need within the firm's main business, so its expected option value likely exceeds the small cost of continued offering.
The wooden display pallet is less aligned with the paper-focused core and likely costlier to carry, but it still broadens the solution set enough to justify retention for now.
This media-oriented quarter-pallet display is somewhat niche and partly overlapping, yet it remains close to the established display business and is therefore still worth keeping.
